title: Every residue class modulo a positive integer has a representative in the symmetric band
statement: For any a and any m > 0 there is a c with c congruent to a modulo m and -m <= c + c <= m. The witness is a % m when (a % m) + (a % m) <= m, and (a % m) - m otherwise. This is the BOUNDED CHOICE OF REPRESENTATIVE that Fermat's descent needs and that the two-squares lane recorded as missing.

formal.statement: theorem Int.exists_centered_representative : ((x0 : Int) -> ((x1 : Int) -> ((x2 : Int.lt Int.zero x1) -> Exists.{1} Int (fun (x3 : Int) => And (Int.ModEq x1 x3 x0) (And (Int.le (Int.neg x1) (Int.add x3 x3)) (Int.le (Int.add x3 x3) x1))))))

evidence.notes: Relevant test: the_centered_representative_keeps_the_small_residue_and_shifts_the_large_one. At m = 5 it pins BOTH branches -- 7 % 5 = 2 is kept, 8 % 5 = 3 must shift to -2, and c = 3 is REFUSED. Nothing else distinguishes the two branches: a construction that returned the bare remainder in both would pass the first row and fail the third. A fourth row requires 7 to be NOT congruent to -2 modulo 5, so the congruence conjunct is not vacuous either.

notes: No decidable if and no Int.bmod definition: Int.le_total supplies the split as an Or and BOTH branches build a witness, so the construction is a plain Or.elim into Exists.intro. Declaring a centered-remainder FUNCTION would have needed a Decidable instance for Int.le that this prelude does not have. Every bound here is spelled Int.add c c and NOT Int.mul (ofNat 2) c. The two are equal and the mul form reads closer to the textbook, but the add form is the one the existing shelf can MOVE: doubling an inequality is then literally Int.add_le_add h h, with no 0 <= 2 side condition and no numeral for ring::int to normalise. This is not a weakening -- 2*|c| <= m and -m <= c+c <= m are the same statement about c.
